correctness.rationale: The identity T(2^k)=2^(k-1)(2^k+1) and the unique involution modulo odd prime powers prove the necessary-and-sufficient odd-exponent order criterion. The 13 smaller 3-coprime candidate indices are ruled out by explicit prime-order witnesses, and ord_11(2)=10, ord_43(2)=14 give k=35 mod70 for T(43)=946. The complete lists of triangular divisors for each odd exponent k=1..35 follow from exhaustive prime-power divisor enumeration and the exact test 8d+1=(2j+1)^2. The k=35 eight-element interval has Möbius values (1,-1,0,0,0,-1,0,1); for 3<=k<=33 odd, the cone under T(2)=3 makes all other proper Möbius values zero. The attached verifier reran 18 complete intervals and 3822 direct/order comparisons. It does not replace the symbolic infinite proof.

value.rationale: The Möbius function of triangular-number divisibility is an explicitly studied arithmetic-poset invariant; the odd dyadic subsequence is a natural structured family. The structural order criterion holds for all triangular divisors and all odd dyadic exponents. It identifies a previously unrecognized 3-coprime divisor appearing first at a surprising exponent 35 and recurring periodically, and explains the first positive Möbius value on the odd-exponent subfamily beyond k=1. The exact finite cutoff is motivated by the complete divisor-order mechanism rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical sample. No general asymptotic result is asserted.
